acceptanceCriteria: report.json latency metrics carry load averages, logical CPU count and run-queue length (where available) for each sampling window; absent fields are recorded as NOT_OBSERVED, not zero.
A latency-only failure under recorded contention above a declared threshold yields a distinct typed outcome (retry-later) separate from a latency regression; focused tests cover both.
Spec requirement and build-log entry recorded; Closes #1406.
body: GitHub #1406: native agent-host qualification (internal/opencodequalification) failed three tries only on lifecycle p95 (267-310 ms vs 250 ms limit) at host load ~11.5; report.json records latencyMethod, per-attempt p95 and sample counts but no load averages, logical CPU count, run-queue/steal, or a same-window baseline, so a contended host reports UNQUALIFIED with no way to tell a regression from contention. Requested: record contention per sampling window, a same-window baseline, and a distinct outcome for latency failures under recorded contention.

completion.reason: ALREADY-DELIVERED: #1413 (commit 4692b0071, on origin/main) records host contention and a same-window baseline in host qualification latency. Verified by ghissues-1021q lane (PR #1494). Live Linux/OpenCode qualification remains V1-2201.

title: GH #1406: host qualification latency records host contention and a same-window baseline instead of bare absolute p95 limits
